PEP 8 — Style Guide for Python Code

This document gives coding conventions for the Python code comprising the standard library in the main Python distribution.

Indentation: use 4 spaces per indentation level and no tabs. Continuation lines should align wrapped elements vertically or use a hanging indent of four extra spaces.

Naming conventions: modules should have short, all-lowercase names; classes should use the CapWords convention; functions should be lowercase with underscores between words.

Imports should usually be on separate lines and placed at the top of the file, just after any module comments and docstrings, and before module globals and constants.
